messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: SLO_BREACH streaming.generate.p99 > 1.0s (current=1.82s). affected_pool=shared-gpu-3. paging oncall group: eng-oncall.
oncall-alex: I'm oncall — acknowledging. any customer-facing alerts yet? :eyes:
sre-jordan: looking at grafana now — p95 ~420ms, p99 spikes to ~1.8s across the last 7m. traces show a lot of streaming stalls (idle stalls + stalled writes). link: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/streaming/streaming-latency?panelId=7&orgId=1
sre-jordan: quick snapshot: io_ops/s on shared-gpu-3 NVMe: 4.2k -> 18k. blkio throttled_time increased heavily for cgroup tenants: tenant_cgroup=tenant:4567
oncall-alex: any noisy tenants obvious? can we identify top producers by io/s?
sre-jordan: ran this prom query: 
```
topk(10, sum(rate(node_disk_io_time_seconds_total[1m])) by (tenant))
```
shows tenant:4567 and tenant:9987 as top two. tenant:4567 has sustained large sequential writes ~200MB/s.
infra-ops: copying PCIe/blkio stats to /tmp for postmortem. also seeing high kv-cache miss rate for those tenants (cache pressure) — that increases read amplification.
support-lee: CS reports 3 customers in EU/APAC flagged streaming stalls (logs show reconnects and partial chunks). I'm pinging account owners.
oncall-alex: mitigation plan: 1) quick throttles on suspected noisy tenants 2) move heavy tenants to iso-gpu pool if throttles insufficient 3) if needed, temporarily reduce streaming batch size for shared pool. I'll execute step 1 now.
infra-ops: agree. ready for throttle commands.
oncall-alex: running throttle now: 
```
echo 200 > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/tenant_4567/blkio.weight
echo 200 > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/tenant_9987/blkio.weight
```
(we normally keep weight=500 for production tenants)
sre-jordan: applied. monitoring...
(2m)
sre-jordan: immediate signal: p99 dropped from 1.82s -> 1.12s after throttle. io/s for tenant:4567 dropped ~60%.
pm-rita: any downstream customer retries/errors? we should prepare a short status note.
support-lee: tickets: #2349 (Acme) had reconnects at 14:03 UTC, #2350 (Nimbus) saw chunk timeouts around same window. I've sent initial status messages.
eng-runtime-bot: Deploy notice: rolling patch to reduce default streaming.large_chunk_size from 4MB -> 2MB has been staged to shared-gpu-3 (canary=10%). will monitor error rate.
(internally) infra-ops: planning live migration for tenant:4567 — moving to iso-gpu-2. will use live-migrate script that schedules minimal restarts. queuing migration job. ETA ~ 12m.
(oncall-alex) thanks. please confirm migration window and expected disruption.
infra-ops: migration started at 2468001267. expected short reconnects (~<10s) for active streams while socket flaps during warmup. will try to drain gracefully.
sre-jordan: metrics during migration: p99 now ~0.95s (below SLO), streaming stalls reduced significantly. trace link: https://tracing.redwood/trace/abc123
oncall-alex: good. mark mitigation success if no regression in next 10m. continuing to watch.
(8m)
support-lee: customer update sent: "We've mitigated an infrastructure issue causing elevated streaming latency; some streams experienced brief reconnects. We're following up and will share a detailed incident report."
pm-rita: rough impact calc: ~12% of streaming calls in shared-gpu-3 had elevated latency or retries during the 14m window. marking as P2.
infra-ops: migration finished at 2468001330. tenant:4567 now on iso-gpu-2. blkio stats isolated.
sre-jordan: post-migration metrics: p99 steady ~0.88s, p95 ~380ms. no further throttling needed.
oncall-alex: handoff: I'm handing this to infra-ops for follow-up (data collection, root cause, remediation). infra-ops please own until M-8h.
infra-ops: taking ownership. collecting: fio traces, blkio.throttle stats, kernel logs, perf top samples from migration period. will schedule tenant audit and enforce IO QoS limits on shared pool.
sre-jordan: notes for postmortem: suspects: tenant background prefetch + KV cache misses causing sustained sequential writes -> NVMe queue saturation -> cgroup throttle and kernel IO wait -> streaming stalls. action items: (1) tighten per-tenant IO caps in shared pool (2) add alert on sustained sequential write rate per-tenant (3) improve canary for streaming.large_chunk_size rollout.
oncall-alex: closing incident for oncall rotation. if infra finds deeper cause, reopen or file follow-up incident. thanks all. :tada:
support-lee: I'll sync with CS for targeted customer follow-ups tomorrow.
infra-ops: leaving handover doc in /incidents/handovers/2468001234-handoff.md and will attach logs.
sre-jordan: adding timeline and perf dumps to the ticket.
eng-runtime-bot: NOTE: we flagged the canary deploy and rolled back large_chunk_size change on shared-gpu-3 during mitigation window to avoid confounding factors.
(oncall-alex) signoff at 2468001399.
